questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
My original destination, New Zealand, was cancelled due to COVID-19.
Learning the german language and learning about the german academic tradition as well as german society, culture and history. Getting international friends was important to me as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most information was easy to find, it was mainly hard to find information on the whole process of choosing courses, how to register and how many ECTS-credits they would give, they have another system in Heidelberg.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Information on what to do was provided via e-mail. I just had to print a lot of documents, get them signed and deliver them to a mail box.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I filled out an application, with different housing options with different cost categories through the "Studierendenwerk" and was lucky enough to get an apartment.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A very basic kitchen with two heat plates, no oven or microwave and without functioning ventilation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: My apartment was cheap and in a correspondingly bad state. It was also very unclean when I moved in.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was really hard to navigate the system and getting information because every professor runs their courses differently and you have to contact them directly, and off course you might not get an answer.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Depends on the course, the professors might have different processes for their courses. This was really confusing, there was not one standardized procedure like in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Just trying to send e-mails to the administration, but the most effective help was talking to other students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to in the end, but I was unsure until the day the classes had already started.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to Heidelberg a month before the semester starts, take the language course offered in this month. That extra time to get settled in is valuable. Join the buddy programme and ask what is the most sensible thing to do for your study area/faculty.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was still mainly online teaching, so it is hard to give a good review of the courses. My courses were quite focused on memorising a lot of chemistry for the exams without aids, which i found quite demotivating.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were master's level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: My impression is, there is a lot of focus on memorising a lot in the german academic culture. Less mandatory group work/presentations in Heidelberg compared to Copenhagen. Could also just be the courses i chose.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
An introduction to machine learning
Aromaten und Heteroaromaten
Bioinformatics & computational biology
Chemie und Biochemie der Alkaloide
Pharmazeutische Biologie: Arzneipflanzen, biogene Arzneistoffe, Biotechnologie
Pharmazeutische/Medizinische Chemie
Programming Curse with Python for Biologists

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy a lot of kitchen equipment, because I expected that to be there as I was moving into a dormitory.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transportation was more expensive than I expected.
But you can buy a "semester-ticket" for approximately 170 euro with which you can travel in the area of Heidelberg for the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of opportunities for extracurricular language courses, which I enjoyed a lot more than the courses at the university. There are a lot of offers regarding sports and clubs, but i was not active in them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
A lot of Erasmus related events were available, of all kind. 
You can go to the theater often for free when you're a student.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Take part in the language courses at Max Weber Haus.
Go travel to German cities, there are a lot of interesting cities and historical sites around Heidelberg.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go visit the nearby cities (Mannheim, Speyer, Schwetzingen are all a visit worth) and go hiking in Odenwald and Schwarzwald (go see Freiburg as well).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was okay, it helps to take a language course before the semester starts and meet som people. Become friends with at least one person who is german and knows the area, that is a big advantage.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be an extrovert, else its near impossible to get into a group of germans

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, it was just hard to get into an only german speaking class and socialize.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language and history

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open to learning the language and take advantage of the language courses, they are free for erasmus+.
Seek to talk german from the beginning and make use of the many interesting travel destinations in southern germany. 
Don't worry so much about the course registration, you can just show up after they have startet

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to get a room through the "Studierendenwerk" because otherwise it can be difficult to find a room to a reasonable price.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning the language and travelling.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Having courses in german with really challenging exams, and being overburdened with study because the courses give so few ECTS-credits, I had 7 courses to get my 30 ECTS. 
Also trying to get into a german social group at the university was near impossible, but there is always the erasmus-group.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
